answer: Public execution meadow nodes require state-checkpointed transit bonds so agents cannot wander into synthetic routes without collateral. Each identity locks a 20,000 POA bond; a sybil attacker spawning 1,000 fake identities must risk 20,000,000 POA locked upfront compared to an honest agent paying once. Conflicting state submissions trigger immediate slashing: 60% burned, 40% paid to reporting peers, inducing an unsustainable cost spiral and a permanent node ban. However, strict bonding introduces capital centralization and creates cold-start friction for honest newcomers.
